newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page-April 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page-April 30.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on April 30:
WASHINGTON - The stock and bond markets rallied on news that workers' wages and benefits are not rising fast enough to spur inflation despite strong economic growth and tight labor markets.

ABERDEEN PROVING GROUND, Md. - A court-martial jury convicted an Army drill sergeant of raping six soldiers under his command after a sensational trial that exposed rampant sex and abuse of authority at this military base.

DENVER - The wife of one of Timothy McVeigh's closest friends testified that McVeigh told her he planned to bomb an Oklahoma City federal building as "an easy target" and used a "bunch of soup cans" to demonstrate how he would do it.

WASHINGTON - A plan by two billionaires to build an "Internet in the Sky" that would use hundreds of low-orbiting satellites to transmit data and conversations all over the world turned from starry-eyed vision to work-in-progress.

KINSHASA, Zaire - With rebel forces closing in fast on the capital, the eleventh-hour U.S. mediator announced that President Mobutu Sese Seko has agreed to his first meeting with insurgent leader Laurent Kabila.
FREDERICK, Md. - A Nobel prize-winning scientist was sentenced to 18 months in prison for sexually abusing a teen-age boy he brought back with him from one of his research trips to Micronesia.

WASHINGTON - As President Clinton prepared to start his second term last January, he proclaimed in an interview that the 1996 election had settled a great debate about the role of government in his favor. Three months later, there is scant evidence for his claim.
